details: The US Federal Reserve concluded its two-day meeting on July 29, 2026, by maintaining its benchmark interest rate in the target range of 3.50% to 3.75%. Despite the decision to hold rates, three out of twelve Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members dissented, preferring a 0.25% rate hike, signaling internal divisions and a hawkish undertone. The Committee's official statement acknowledged "elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East" and noted that "inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal." Investors are now keenly awaiting Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference for further insights into the future trajectory of monetary policy.
title: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Amid Dissent, Cites Middle East Conflict

details: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have dramatically escalated in the last 24 hours. US and Saudi forces conducted joint retaliatory airstrikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq, reportedly resulting in the deaths of at least 20 fighters and 6 Iranian advisers. This action followed Iranian missile attacks targeting American forces in the region. Jordan's military also reported intercepting five Iranian missiles aimed at its territory. These renewed hostilities have caused oil prices, specifically WTI crude, to surge by over 6% due to intensified concerns over supply disruptions, particularly around the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Adding to the instability, Iran rejected Oman's proposal for joint management of the Strait, further dampening hopes for de-escalation.
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate with US-Saudi Strikes and Iranian Missiles
